diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The location hint points to gaps/ambiguities in d3-visualization/SKILL.md around (1) making chart elements reliably clickable, (2) ensuring text labels are rendered above shapes without blocking pointer events, and (3) defining/verifying robust two-way linkage between a chart and a table. These are core requirements of the task (bubble click highlights table row and vice versa; labels inside bubbles; tooltip behavior), so the skill documentation should be repaired to include concrete, testable guidance and acceptance checks for these behaviors.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill guide’s sections on clickable graphics, text overlay layering, and chart↔table two-way interaction/verification are incomplete or insufficiently prescriptive for deterministic, testable implementations. Common pitfalls likely not covered: text labels intercepting clicks/hover (missing pointer-events:none), z-ordering between circles and labels, using stable keys for selections across chart and table, and explicit acceptance criteria for bidirectional highlight/scroll-into-view behavior.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise/expand the SKILL.md guidance in the specified areas to: (1) prescribe how to make SVG marks reliably clickable (attach handlers to marks or to a <g> wrapper; use pointer cursor; define selected state via classes); (2) specify a safe layering pattern for labels over bubbles (append circles first then text, or separate layers; set text pointer-events:none; ensure accessibility/contrast); (3) provide an explicit pattern for two-way chart↔table linking using a stable key (e.g., ticker), shared state (selectedKey), and update functions that apply/remove CSS classes in both views; and (4) add concrete acceptance/verification checklist items for bidirectional selection, label overlay not blocking interaction, and deterministic updates (use .data(..., keyFn)). Preserve unrelated working content.
